title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States
abstract: arXiv:2611.29768v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study how observed many-body system size affects the number of state copies needed to estimate a zero-temperature first-order transition point. The unknown Hamiltonian has bounded, translation-invariant on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on a 3D cubic lattice with local dimension three. The field coupling is known, and all models share a known boundary field penalizing one local level. The limiting order parameter is uniformly separated across the transition. Each query returns an independently prepared Gibbs or ground state at an adaptive field and system size.   For error $\epsilon$ and fixed confidence, we prove an exponential separation between two size caps at the same temperature. There are absolute constants $00$ such that, at inverse temperature $\beta=c_1/\epsilon$, restricting side lengths to $L\le c_0/\epsilon$ requires $\exp(\Omega(1/\epsilon))$ copies in worst-case expectation, even with collective measurements.

translated_title: 从吉布斯态与基态估计相变点
translated_abstract: 我们研究观测到的多体系统尺寸如何影响估计零温一级相变点所需的状态副本数量。未知的哈密顿量在局部维度为3的三维立方格点上具有有界的、平移不变的局域项和最近邻相互作用。场耦合是已知的，且所有模型共享一个用于惩罚某一局部能级的已知边界场。极限序参量在相变两侧均匀分离。每次查询返回在一个自适应选择的场和系统尺寸下独立制备的吉布斯态或基态。对于误差 $\epsilon$ 和固定置信度，我们证明了在同一温度下两种尺寸上限之间的指数级分离。存在绝对常数 $c_0, c_1>0$，使得在逆温度 $\beta=c_1/\epsilon$ 时，若将边长限制在 $L\le c_0/\epsilon$，则最坏情况期望下需要 $\exp(\Omega(1/\epsilon))$ 个副本，即使允许集体测量也是如此。
tldr: 该论文证明了在估计零温一级相变点时，若将可观测系统的尺寸限制在 $L \le c_0/\epsilon$，即使采用集体测量，所需样本数也会出现 $\exp(\Omega(1/\epsilon))$ 的指数级爆炸，从而揭示了系统尺寸限制对相变点估计复杂度具有决定性的指数级影响。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that estimating a zero-temperature first-order transition point requires exponentially many state copies, exp(Ω(1/ε)) in worst-case expectation even with collective measurements, when the observable system size is capped at L ≤ c₀/ε, revealing an exponential complexity separation driven by system-size restrictions.
